questions.q: A 6-year-old unvaccinated child presents with a 3-day history of high fever, coryza, conjunctivitis, and barking cough. On examination, you notice red macules with white centers on the buccal mucosa opposite the premolar teeth. What is the clinical significance of these intraoral findings?
opts: They represent viral replication in the salivary glands and indicate bacterial superinfection
They are pathognomonic for measles and typically appear 48 hours before the cutaneous exanthem
They are caused by Candida albicans and indicate immunosuppression from measles
They represent permanent scarring of the mucosa and indicate previous measles infection
questions.exp:
Koplik's spots are the characteristic enanthem of measles, appearing as bright red macules with 1–2 mm blue-white ('grains of sand') centers on the buccal mucosa. These pathognomonic findings appear during the prodrome, 48 hours before the exanthem develops, making them clinically useful for early diagnosis. The presence of Koplik's spots confirms measles infection before the typical morbilliform rash becomes apparent.
🏰 Palace: Picture tiny SAND GRAINS (blue-white centers) sprinkled on the MOUTH opposite premolars of a castle—appearing 48 HOURS BEFORE the body rash invades the kingdom.

questions.q: Which cellular receptors does the measles virus primarily utilize for host cell entry during natural infections?
opts: CD46 and CD80
CD150 (SLAM) and nectin 4 (PVRL4)
ACE2 and DPP4
ICAM-1 and LFA-3
questions.exp:
The measles virus uses CD150 (signaling lymphocyte activation molecule, or SLAM) and nectin 4 (poliovirus receptor-like 4, PVRL4) as the specific cellular receptors for host cell entry during natural infections. While cultured laboratory strains can also bind to CD46, this is not the primary receptor used in vivo. Understanding these receptors is important for explaining viral tropism and pathogenesis.
🏰 Palace: In the castle tower labeled CD150, a SLAM DUNK happens when measles virus bounces through NECTIN 4 gates—these are the natural PORTALS of entry, not CD46 the laboratory impostor.

questions.q: A 32-year-old woman with penicillin allergy presents with genital ulcer disease consistent with non-herpetic GUD. Which NACO kit regimen should be administered?
opts: NACO Kit 3: Azithromycin 1 g stat + Benzathine Penicillin 2.4 MU IM
NACO Kit 4: Azithromycin 1 g stat + Doxycycline 100 mg BD for 14–15 days
NACO Kit 5: Acyclovir 400 mg TDS for 7 days
NACO Kit 6: Standard inguinal bubo regimen
questions.exp: NACO Kit 4 (Blue) is specifically designated for non-herpetic GUD in penicillin-allergic patients and contains Azithromycin 1 g stat + Doxycycline 100 mg BD for 14–15 days. Kit 3 contains Benzathine Penicillin which is contraindicated in penicillin-allergic individuals.

questions.q: A 28-year-old woman presents with multiple firm, red nodules covering her scalp that have been slowly growing over several years. Genetic testing reveals a mutation in the CYLD gene on chromosome 16. Which of the following inheritance patterns is most consistent with her condition?
opts: Autosomal recessive inheritance
Autosomal dominant inheritance
X-linked dominant inheritance
Mitochondrial inheritance
questions.exp: Multiple familial trichoepitheliomas are associated with autosomal dominant inheritance patterns and are linked to mutations in the CYLD gene on chromosome 16. This genetic pattern is similar to Brooke-Spiegler syndrome, which involves multiple trichoepitheliomas, cylindromas, and spiradenomas. Sporadic forms may show PTCH1 gene deletions instead.
questions.palace: 🏰 Palace: Picture a DOMINANT CYLD KING sitting on a CHROMOSOME 16 THRONE in the castle, ruling MULTIPLE TRICHOEPITHELIOMA TERRITORIES across his domain—each generation of his heirs inherits his empire (autosomal dominant).

questions.q: A surgeon performing an elliptical excision on the cheek notes tissue puckering at the apices after partial closure. Which of the following is the MOST common geometric cause of dog-ear formation in this scenario?
opts: Apical angles greater than 30° due to an inadequate, short/fat ellipse design
Excessive undermining creating redundant tissue planes
Unilateral excessive suture tension on one wound edge
Infection of the subcutaneous layer during wound healing
questions.exp: Dog-ear formation is primarily caused by geometric factors, particularly apical angles greater than 30° resulting from inadequate ellipse design (short or wide), combined with unequal wound edge lengths. While other factors like inadequate undermining can cause pseudo-dog-ears, the chief geometric culprit is the obtuse apical angle in poorly designed ellipses.

questions.q: A 6-year-old boy with psoriasis develops sudden onset of numerous small papules and plaques (<1 cm) across his trunk and extremities following a streptococcal pharyngitis infection 2 weeks ago. Which psoriasis variant is most likely, and what is its strongest HLA association?
opts: Plaque psoriasis; HLA-B27
Guttate psoriasis; HLA-Cw6
Palmoplantar psoriasis; HLA-DR4
Inverse psoriasis; HLA-A2
questions.exp: Guttate psoriasis is the second most common variant in childhood, representing 6.4% to 44% of cases, and is characteristically triggered by streptococcal infection. Guttate psoriasis carries the absolute strongest association with HLA-Cw6 of all psoriasis variants. 🏰 Palace: Imagine tiny WATER DROPLETS (guttae) made of ICE labeled 'Cw6' falling from storm clouds shaped like STREPTOCOCCAL BALLS — guttate psoriasis and Cw6 are inseparable twins after strep throat.

questions.q: A 28-year-old sexually active woman presents with multiple painful vesicles and shallow ulcers on her labia that appeared 5 days ago, preceded by burning pain and malaise. She also has painful inguinal lymphadenopathy. What is the most likely diagnosis?
opts: Primary syphilis (chancre)
Herpes simplex virus (HSV) genital infection
Lymphogranuloma venereum (LGV)
Donovanosis (granuloma inguinale)
questions.exp: HSV is the most common cause of painful genital ulcers globally. The presentation of multiple painful vesicles progressing to shallow ulcers with systemic symptoms (malaise) and painful lymphadenopathy is classic for primary HSV infection. In contrast, syphilitic chancres are typically solitary, indurated, and painless; LGV presents with a transient painless papule; and donovanosis presents as beefy-red, slowly progressive, painless lesions.

questions.q: A patient presents with a persistent dog-ear at the apex of a forehead scar 2 months post-excision. The surgeon wishes to repair it while avoiding extension across cosmetic boundaries. Which technique is MOST appropriate for this anatomic location?
opts: Classic straight-line Burow's triangle excision extended along the original scar
Hockey stick/L-plasty technique to redirect the scar direction
Unequal suturing using the rule of halves redistribution method
Fusiform extension of the original ellipse at the time of initial closure
questions.exp: The hockey stick or L-plasty technique is specifically designed to avoid extending the scar in a straight line when repair would cross cosmetic boundaries, making it ideal for the forehead where directional changes preserve cosmetic subunits. The angled incision effectively redirects tension and shortens the overall scar length compared to straight-line closure.

questions.q: A 10-month-old infant presents with a 6-day fever, strawberry tongue, conjunctival injection, and cervical lymphadenopathy. Laboratory work shows ESR 52 mm/h and CRP 4.2 mg/dL, but echocardiography reveals coronary artery dilatation. Which classification best describes this presentation and why is it clinically significant?
opts: Classic Kawasaki Disease; presents with all 5 mucocutaneous criteria and requires immediate IVIg
Incomplete Kawasaki Disease; most common in infants <6 months and carries highest risk for severe coronary sequelae due to delayed diagnosis
Adult-Onset Kawasaki Disease; requires screening for HIV co-infection as part of workup
Multisystem Inflammatory Syndrome in Children; triggered by SARS-CoV-2 rather than an unknown respiratory pathogen
questions.exp: Incomplete Kawasaki Disease presents with prolonged fever (≥5 days) plus only 2–3 mucocutaneous features, confirmed by supportive labs (ESR ≥40 mm/h, CRP ≥3.0 mg/dL) or coronary abnormalities on echocardiography. Infants <6 months are paradoxically at highest risk for severe coronary aneurysms because the incomplete presentation often delays life-saving IVIg therapy.
questions.memory: 🏰 Palace: A tiny BABY (6 months) in the castle's SMALLEST ROOM carries the BIGGEST TREASURE (coronary aneurysm risk)—incomplete symptoms lock the door to early IVIg rescue.

questions.q: A term infant (3.5 kg) presents with scattered erythematous macules and pustules on the cheeks, chest and trunk at 36 hours of life. Smear cytology shows predominantly eosinophils with no organisms. Which of the following best explains the epidemiological pattern of this eruption?
opts: It reflects maternal IgE-mediated allergic sensitization transferred across the placenta
It is a localized innate-immune response to commensal skin microbes colonizing the newborn after birth
It is caused by transplacental transfer of pathogenic maternal lymphocytes that attack fetal skin
It occurs exclusively in premature infants and indicates systemic infection requiring immediate antibiotics
questions.exp:
Erythema toxicum neonatorum is a benign, self-limiting eruption of healthy term infants (>2500 g) that typically begins 24–48 hours after delivery. The prevailing etiopathogenesis is a localized innate-immune response to commensal microbes colonizing the newborn's skin after birth, triggering acute-phase inflammation with IL-1α, IL-8, eotaxin, and tryptase-expressing perifollicular mast cells. The historical graft-versus-host hypothesis (maternal lymphocyte transfer) has been disproven, and there is no toxic or infectious component. Pustular eruptions in preterm infants should prompt evaluation for systemic infection, but ETN is a disease of healthy full-term neonates.
🏰 Palace: Walk into a NEWBORN NURSERY (birth = 24–48 hrs) where FRIENDLY COMMENSALS are throwing an IMMUNE PARTY (localized innate response) in the skin's HAIR FOLLICLES—not a toxic attack or maternal lymphocyte invasion.
questions.source: [Paeds Day 1] Transient Neonatal Pustular and Vesicular Eruptions

questions.q: A premature neonate weighing 850 g born at 26 weeks' gestation develops a massive 'burn-like' exfoliative erythroderma with weeping erosions on day 3 of life. Blood cultures grow Candida albicans. Which layer of the epidermis is characteristically spared of fungal invasion in congenital cutaneous candidiasis, but is involved in this systemic variant?
opts: Stratum corneum only
Deep dermis and subcutaneous tissue with systemic visceral seeding
Stratum lucidum exclusively
Granular layer with basal layer involvement
questions.exp: In congenital cutaneous candidiasis affecting healthy term infants, fungal elements are strictly confined to the stratum corneum with intraepidermal microabscesses. However, in invasive/systemic congenital candidiasis in very-low-birth-weight premature neonates, widespread dissemination occurs to deep viscera (lungs, liver, spleen, CNS) with cutaneous manifestation as severe exfoliative erythroderma rather than discrete pustules. This reflects penetration beyond the superficial epidermis.
questions.palace: 🏰 Palace: A TINY PREMATURE BABY (850g) stands naked in the castle courtyard—his STRATUM CORNEUM armor is stripped away, exposing the DEEP DUNGEONS beneath (liver, lungs, spinal cord tower) to invading CANDIDA ARMIES, creating a weeping BURN-like wasteland across his kingdom.

questions.q: A 2-day-old Black neonate presents with a poorly circumscribed, grayish-blue macular patch over the lumbosacral region measuring 8 cm in diameter. The mother is concerned about this appearance. Which optical phenomenon best explains the characteristic bluish hue of this lesion?
opts: Rayleigh scattering of longer wavelengths by superficial epidermal melanin
Tyndall effect causing preferential scattering of shorter blue light wavelengths by deep dermal melanin
Mie scattering from collagen bundles in the reticular dermis
Absorption of red and green light by catalase-positive melanocytes
questions.exp: The characteristic bluish-gray hue of a classic Mongolian spot is caused by the Tyndall effect, in which shorter wavelengths of visible light (blue) are scattered back to the observer's eye by melanin granules located deep in the dermis, while longer wavelengths penetrate deeper. This optical phenomenon is the defining reason why Mongolian spots appear blue rather than the brown color expected from dermal melanin.

questions.q: On histopathology of a skin biopsy from a suspected cutaneous wart, which cell finding is considered pathognomonic for active HPV infection?
opts: Increased melanin deposition in the basal layer with preserved dermatoglyphic lines
Koilocytes with distinct perinuclear cytoplasmic vacuolization surrounding a hyperchromatic, pyknotic, raisinoid nucleus
Ballooned keratinocytes without nuclear changes located exclusively in the granular layer
Increased mitotic figures with atypical spindle cells in the deep dermis
questions.exp: Koilocytes are the pathognomonic histopathologic hallmark of HPV infection. These enlarged, atypical keratinocytes exhibit a distinct clear halo (perinuclear cytoplasmic vacuolization) surrounding a hyperchromatic, shrunken, pyknotic, or wrinkled ("raisinoid") nucleus, representing the viral cytopathic effect of active viral assembly. Koilocytes are typically found in the upper spinous and granular layers and may be accompanied by basophilic nuclear inclusions.
questions.memory: 🏰 Palace: Picture a RAISIN (shrunken nucleus) floating in a CLEAR HALO MOAT inside the KOILOCYTE CASTLE—this RAISIN-IN-A-HALO is the ROYAL SEAL of active HPV viral assembly in the UPPER SPINOUS TOWER.

questions.q: A dermoscopic examination of a suspected basal cell carcinoma reveals a pigmented lesion with brown spoke-wheel structures. Which BCC subtype is this finding MOST heavily associated with?
opts: Nodular BCC with arborizing telangiectasias
Superficial BCC
Infiltrative/morpheaform BCC
Pigmented BCC (with white or brown spoke-wheel pattern)
questions.exp: White or brown spoke-wheel structures (well-defined radial projections extending from a central darker hub) are highly specific for pigmented BCC according to the note. These structures represent a characteristic feature distinguishing pigmented BCC from other BCC subtypes, which would show different dermoscopic patterns such as arborizing vessels in nodular or erosions in superficial variants.
questions.🏰 Palace: 🏰 Imagine a BROWN WHEEL (spoke-wheel) spinning in the center of a PIGMENTED palace—this wheel is the trademark of pigmented BCC, distinct from all other subtypes.

questions.q: A 32-year-old man with a history of unprotected sex presents with a solitary, well-demarcated, indurated ulcer on his glans penis that is completely painless. Dark-field microscopy and RPR are pending. What is the most likely diagnosis, and what is the key clinical feature distinguishing this from other common GUD causes?
opts: Chancroid; distinguished by painful, ragged, undermined edges with purulent exudate
Primary syphilis; distinguished by being solitary, indurated, and painless
Herpes simplex virus; distinguished by multiple painful vesicles progressing to shallow erosions
Donovanosis; distinguished by slowly progressive, beefy-red appearance
questions.exp: The primary chancre of syphilis classically presents as a solitary, indurated, and painless ulcer—a key distinguishing feature from HSV (multiple, painful), chancroid (ragged, purulent), and donovanosis (beefy-red, slowly progressive). The painless nature and singular presentation are classic hallmarks that should prompt serological testing with RPR/VDRL and treponemal confirmation.

questions.q: A 3-week-old Hispanic infant is found to have extensive Mongolian spots covering the trunk, shoulders, and extremities with a confetti appearance, and the lesions appear darker than typical sacral spots. Which underlying condition should be immediately investigated given this atypical presentation?
opts: Neurofibromatosis type 1 with café-au-lait macules
Inborn errors of metabolism, particularly lysosomal storage diseases such as GM1 gangliosidosis or Hurler disease
Phakomatosis pigmentovascularis exclusively caused by germline mutations in TP53
Familial progressive hyperpigmentation due to CDKN2A mutations
questions.exp: Extensive, dark, and progressive Mongolian spots extending far beyond the classic lumbosacral distribution are a major cutaneous red flag for underlying inborn errors of metabolism, particularly lysosomal storage diseases including GM1 gangliosidosis type 1, Hurler disease (MPS I), Hunter disease (MPS II), Niemann-Pick disease, and mucolipidosis II. Classic solitary Mongolian spots require no further workup, but extensive variants demand metabolic screening.

questions.q: A 2-day-old full-term neonate presents with discrete vesicles and pustules on an erythematous base affecting the trunk, extremities, palms, and soles. The placenta shows focal yellow-white microabscesses. Which immunological pathway is primarily responsible for protective mucocutaneous immunity against this infection?
opts: Dectin-1/TLR2 → CARD9 → Th17 differentiation → IL-17 production
CD8+ cytotoxic T cells → perforin-mediated apoptosis
B cells → IgG opsonization → complement activation
Natural killer cells → interferon-gamma production
questions.exp: The host's innate immune defense against Candida is triggered when pattern recognition receptors Dectin-1 and TLR2 bind to β-glucan and mannan on the fungal cell wall, activating the CARD9 signaling adaptor. This leads to Th17 cell differentiation and IL-17 production, which is absolutely critical for mucocutaneous defense against Candida. IL-17 is the key cytokine that prevents dissemination in cutaneous candidiasis.
questions.palace: 🏰 Palace: Imagine DECTIN guards at the castle gate (TLR2 sentinels) spotting BETA-GLUCAN INVADERS, triggering CARD9 knights to summon SEVENTEEN IL-17 ARMIES that march through town halls (Th17 fortress) to defend the MUCOCUTANEOUS moat.

questions.q: A 35-year-old woman presents with a subclinical cervical HPV infection. During colposcopy, 3–5% acetic acid is applied to the cervix for 3–5 minutes. Which of the following best describes the expected finding and its clinical significance?
opts: Acetowhitening is pathognomonic for HPV infection and reliably predicts cervical cancer risk without further evaluation

Acetowhitening highlights abnormal epithelium but lacks specificity, as inflammatory conditions like candidiasis and lichen planus can produce similar white appearance, necessitating biopsy for confirmation
Acetowhitening is used to screen for HPV in asymptomatic patients and definitively rules out intraepithelial neoplasia
Acetowhitening is most useful for distinguishing between low-risk and high-risk HPV genotypes on the cervix
questions.exp: Acetic acid (3–5%) causes acetowhitening of abnormal epithelium in subclinical HPV infections, but this finding is not specific to HPV and can occur with other inflammatory conditions such as candidiasis, psoriasis, and lichen planus. Therefore, acetowhite lesions identified during colposcopy or high-resolution anoscopy require tissue biopsy to guide diagnosis and rule out intraepithelial neoplasia or malignancy rather than being treated empirically based on appearance alone.
questions.memory: 🏰 Palace: Imagine a CASTLE where the ACETIC ACID GUARD (3–5%) turns WALLS WHITE—but the same WHITE PAINT also appears on the CANDIDA TAVERN and LICHEN LIBRARY. The KING demands a BIOPSY SCROLL before believing it's truly HPV's handiwork.

questions.q: A 65-year-old patient presents with a pearlescent nodule on the nose featuring a rolled border and surface telangiectasias. Dermoscopy is performed to confirm the diagnosis. Which of the following dermoscopic features is MOST sensitive and specific for nodular basal cell carcinoma?
opts: Multiple blue-gray globules separated from larger ovoid nests
Arborizing telangiectasias with tree-like branching vessels
Leaf-like areas with radial projections from a central hub
Short, fine superficial telangiectasias with multiple small erosions
questions.exp: Arborizing telangiectasias are described as bright red, large, tree-like branching vessels that focus sharply at the surface and represent the most sensitive and specific dermoscopic feature for nodular BCC. The other features are associated with pigmented BCC (leaf-like areas), multiple blue-gray structures, or superficial BCC variants, making them less characteristic of the nodular type.
questions.🏰 Palace: 🏰 Imagine a NODULAR PALACE made of TREE BRANCHES (arborizing) glowing bright RED like fire vessels—this is the signature feature you cannot miss for nodular BCC.

questions.q: A genetic study is performed on a 2-year-old with systemic mastocytosis and a 40-year-old adult with indolent systemic mastocytosis. The child's KIT mutation is found in exon 11, while the adult carries a D816V point mutation in exon 17. Which statement correctly describes the genetic heterogeneity between these two cases?
opts: Children are more likely to have D816V mutations than adults, making pediatric disease more aggressive
Children show greater genetic diversity with up to 44% having mutations outside exon 17, while 80-90% of adults carry the D816V mutation
Both age groups show identical mutation patterns, and differences reflect only disease severity
The D816V mutation in adults is associated with better prognosis than extracellular domain mutations in children
questions.exp: Pediatric mastocytosis demonstrates greater genetic heterogeneity compared to adults. While 80-90% of adults possess the classic D816V point mutation in exon 17, only 42% of children carry this mutation, and up to 44% harbor mutations outside exon 17 in extracellular or transmembrane domains (exons 8-11). This genetic diversity in children contributes to their often more favorable prognosis.

questions.q: A 7-year-old girl presents with sharply demarcated, symmetrically distributed erythematous plaques on her elbows and knees with silvery-white scales. Histopathology shows marked epidermal acanthosis with elongated rete ridges, absent granular layer, and collections of neutrophils in the stratum corneum. Which HLA allele is most strongly associated with her early-onset plaque psoriasis?
opts: HLA-B27
HLA-Cw6 (HLA-C*06:02)
HLA-DR4
HLA-A2
questions.exp: Early-onset plaque psoriasis (Type I) in children is strongly and almost invariably associated with the HLA-Cw6 allele located at the PSORS1 locus on chromosome 6p21. This HLA association is particularly strong in childhood-onset disease and explains the genetic predisposition in this case. 🏰 Palace: Picture a CHILD wearing a CROWN labeled 'Cw6' standing at the entrance of a CASTLE labeled 'PSORS1 on chromosome 6' — early-onset plaque psoriasis bows to the Cw6 royalty.

questions.q: A 2-day-old Caucasian infant has the classic 'flea-bitten' appearance with firm 1–3 mm papules topped by pale-yellow pustules surrounded by irregular erythematous halos. The eruption began on the cheeks and now involves the face, chest and buttocks, but notably spares the palms and soles. What is the approximate incidence of this condition in full-term healthy neonates?
questions.exp:
Erythema toxicum neonatorum is extremely common, affecting roughly 48–72% of full-term newborns (reported incidence ranges 16.7–55%). The condition is restricted to healthy infants over 2500 g and is rare in premature or low-birth-weight neonates. The classic presentation includes the 'flea-bitten' appearance (central papule/pustule surrounded by a sea of erythema), profuse sparing of palms and soles, and highly transient lesions that migrate and rarely persist >24 hours.
🏰 Palace: Nearly HALF THE NURSERY (48–72%) of healthy FULL-TERM BABIES gets the 'FLEA-BITTEN' look—but their PALMS and SOLES are like PROTECTED ROYAL CHAMBERS where the eruption NEVER dares enter.
questions.source: [Paeds Day 1] Transient Neonatal Pustular and Vesicular Eruptions

questions.q: A 3-year-old child presents with multiple reddish-brown macules and papules on the trunk and thighs. On examination, stroking one of the lesions results in immediate localized whealing and erythema. Histopathology reveals a 40-fold increase in mast cells in the papillary dermis with increased melanin in the basal layer. Which receptor expressed on these clonal mast cells distinguishes them from normal reactive mast cells?
opts: CD34 and HLA-DR
CD25 and/or CD2
CD19 and CD20
CD3 and CD4
questions.exp: In mastocytosis, clonally aberrant mast cells uniquely express the cell-surface receptors CD25 and/or CD2, which are strictly absent on normal reactive mast cells. These markers, along with KIT (CD117), help identify neoplastic mast cells. The positive Darier's sign and histological findings confirm cutaneous mastocytosis with maculopapular variant (urticaria pigmentosa).

questions.q: Regarding the pathogenesis of Kawasaki Disease, which of the following best explains why no specific host autoantigen has been identified despite its classification as a vasculitic syndrome?
opts: The disease results from direct autoantibodies against desmoglein proteins on vascular endothelium, similar to pemphigus

Kawasaki Disease is triggered by a ubiquitous, unidentified infectious agent (likely respiratory virus) causing aberrant immune hyper-reaction in genetically susceptible hosts, with IgA antibodies binding intracellular viral inclusions rather than host tissue
The causative agent is always Staphylococcus aureus producing a superantigen that directly cleaves vascular smooth muscle proteins
It is exclusively an adult disease linked to HIV immunosuppression, making host autoantigen identification impossible in the pediatric population
questions.exp: Kawasaki Disease lacks a known host autoantigen because it is not a primary autoimmune disease targeting specific tissue receptors. Instead, oligoclonal IgA antibodies from KD patients bind intracellular RNA- and protein-containing inclusions within ciliated bronchial epithelium and macrophages, strongly suggesting infection by an intracellular pathogen triggers the systemic vasculitis through aberrant immune activation.
questions.memory: 🏰 Palace: Inside the castle's HIDDEN CHAMBERS (intracellular inclusions), a MYSTERIOUS GHOST (unknown virus) hides—the guards (IgA antibodies) chase the GHOST, not the CASTLE WALLS (no host autoantigen).

questions.q: On histopathology, a solitary skin-colored papule from the nose of a 32-year-old man shows basaloid cell lobules arranged in a cribriform pattern with a prominent fibrocytic stroma containing clefts without retraction artifact. Which histologic feature most specifically helps distinguish this lesion from basal cell carcinoma?
opts: Presence of basaloid cells in the dermis
Cribriform arrangement of neoplastic cells
Tightly adherent stroma to follicular germinative cells with clefts lacking retraction artifact
Papillary mesenchymal bodies
questions.exp: The key distinguishing feature of trichoepithelioma from basal cell carcinoma is that the fibrocytic stroma maintains tightly adherent contact to follicular germinative cells and contains clefts without retraction artifact, whereas basal cell carcinoma typically shows stromal retraction artifact. This stromal relationship, along with the conspicuous fibrocytic stroma that can comprise up to half the lesion's cellularity, is pathognomonic for trichoepithelioma.
questions.palace: 🏰 Palace: Imagine a TIGHT VELCRO BOND (trichoepithelioma stroma) clinging CLEFT-TIGHT to follicular cells WITHOUT PULLING BACK—like a loyal courtier never retreating from the king, unlike the PEELING-BACK TRAITOR (BCC retraction artifact) abandoning the castle walls.

questions.q: A 2-year-old from Japan with xeroderma pigmentosum develops severe xerosis, poikiloderma, and early signs of neurological decline including developmental delay. Which complementation group accounts for approximately 90% of XP cases in this population?
opts: XP-B (ERCC3/XPB helicase defect)
XP-A (XPA damage verification defect)
XP-Variant (translesion synthesis defect)
XP-C (XPC damage recognition defect)
questions.exp: XP-A is the most common complementation group in Japan, accounting for approximately 90% of cases due to a specific founder mutation. XP-A represents a highly severe subtype characterized by acute blistering sunburns with minimal sun exposure and the risk of severe neurodegeneration, including De Sanctis-Cacchione Syndrome when complete loss-of-function mutations are present.
questions.🏰: 🏰 Palace: In the JAPANESE CASTLE, 90% of XP patients have the ANCESTOR'S CURSE—a founder mutation in XPA. The MOST SEVERE form lurks in this ancient lineage, with MASSIVE sun sensitivity and NEUROLOGICAL COLLAPSE.

questions.q: A 28-year-old man presents with urethral discharge. According to WHO guidelines for syndromic management, what is the recommended initial dual therapy to cover both Neisseria gonorrhoeae and Chlamydia trachomatis?
opts: Ceftriaxone 250 mg IM stat + Doxycycline 100 mg BD for 7 days
Cefixime 400 mg PO stat + Azithromycin 1 g PO stat
Metronidazole 2 g stat + Azithromycin 1 g PO stat
Ciprofloxacin 500 mg BD × 3 days + Ceftriaxone 250 mg IM
questions.exp: WHO guidelines recommend dual therapy with either Ceftriaxone 250 mg IM stat (or Cefixime 400 mg PO stat) PLUS Azithromycin 1 g PO stat or Doxycycline 100 mg BD for 7 days to cover both organisms. NACO Kit 1 specifically uses Azithromycin 1 g PO stat + Cefixime 400 mg PO stat for urethral discharge.

questions.q: A 3-year-old boy with xeroderma pigmentosum presents with severe blistering sunburns after minimal sun exposure and progressive neurological decline. Genetic testing reveals mutations in the XPA gene. Which of the following best explains the pathophysiological basis of his condition?
opts: Loss of function in the XPA protein prevents DNA damage verification in the nucleotide excision repair pathway, leading to accumulation of unrepaired UV-induced photoproducts
Autoimmune destruction of melanocytes mediated by anti-tyrosinase antibodies and HLA-associated immune complexes
Defective translesion synthesis polymerase unable to bypass cyclobutane pyrimidine dimers during DNA replication
Impaired melanin synthesis resulting in photosensitivity and secondary autoimmune neurodegeneration
questions.exp: Xeroderma pigmentosum is a disorder of genomic DNA repair, NOT autoimmunity. XPA protein is responsible for damage verification in nucleotide excision repair (NER), specifically recognizing and signaling the presence of UV-induced lesions like cyclobutane pyrimidine dimers (CPDs) and pyrimidine (6-4) pyrimidone photoproducts. Without functional XPA, these lesions accumulate, causing genomic instability and premature carcinogenesis.
questions.🏰: 🏰 Palace: Picture a CASTLE GUARD (XPA protein) at the DNA GATE, scanning for UV DAMAGE BOMBS (CPDs). When the guard is absent, bombs pile up UNDETECTED, causing the kingdom to CRUMBLE with mutations and cancer.
